{{Short description|None}}
{{See also|National team appearances in the FIFA World Cup}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2022}}
As of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026 edition]], 84 national teams have competed at the finals of the men's [[FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |date=14 November 2022 |title=The FIFA World Cup in numbers |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2022/11/14/the-fifa-world-cup-in-numbers |access-date=25 November 2022 |website=Al Jazeera English}}</ref> [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] is the only team to have appeared in all 23 tournaments to date, with [[Germany national football team|Germany]] having participated in 21, [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in 19, and [[Italy national football team|Italy]] and [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] both in 18.<ref name="participations">{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/fifa-tournaments/statistics-and-records/worldcup/teams/index.html#participations |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151007165059/http://www.fifa.com/fifa-tournaments/statistics-and-records/worldcup/teams/index.html#participations |url-status=dead |archive-date=7 October 2015 |title=FIFA World Cup Teams Statistics: Teams with the most tournament participations |publisher=FIFA |access-date=26 June 2018 }}</ref> Eight nations have won the tournament. The inaugural winners in 1930 were [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]]; the current champions are [[Spain national football team|Spain]]. The most successful nation is Brazil, which has won the cup on five occasions.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.businessinsider.com/who-has-won-world-cup-2018-5 |title=The 2018 World Cup is only 2 weeks away — here's who has won every tournament since 1930 |last=Dawson |first=Alan |work=[[Business Insider]] |date=28 May 2018 |access-date=26 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180528113655/http://www.businessinsider.com/who-has-won-world-cup-2018-5 |archive-date=28 May 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Five teams have appeared in [[List of FIFA World Cup finals|FIFA World Cup finals]] without winning,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43956267 |title=World Cup 2018: Can you name the losing finalists from previous tournaments? |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=9 June 2018 |access-date=26 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190508100953/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/43956267 |archive-date=8 May 2019 |url-status=live }}</ref> while twelve more have appeared in the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesw/wcq-records.html |title=World Cup All-Time Tables (including Qualifying) |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=26 June 2018 }}</ref>

=== Overall team records ===
<onlyinclude>The system used in the World Cup up to 1990 was 2 points for a win. In this ranking [[Three points for a win|3 points are awarded for a win]], 1 for a draw, and 0 for a loss. Per statistical convention in football, matches decided in [[extra time (association football)|extra time]] are counted as wins and losses, while matches decided by [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-outs]] are counted as draws. Teams are ranked by total points, then by goal difference, then by goals scored.<ref name="all_time">{{cite web |title=World Cup » All-time league table |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co139/records-all-time-table/ |access-date=14 December 2021 |publisher=worldfootball.net}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Stokkermans |first=Karel |date=9 November 2025 |title=The Twenty-Two Tourneys Till Two Thousand Twenty-Two Total Table 1930-2022 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tables/3002f.html#22tt |access-date=24 December 2022 |website=[[RSSSF]]}}</ref>

|15||align="left" |{{fb|SRB}}{{refn|group="note"|name=YugoslaviaNFT|The [[Yugoslavia national football team]] qualified eight times during eras of [[Kingdom of Yugoslavia]] (1930) and the [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia]] (1950–1990). They qualified from 1930–1990 under the name Yugoslavia before its [[Yugoslavia#Breakup|breakup]] in 1992 by the secession of many of its constituent republics. They qualified once in 1998 as the [[Serbia and Montenegro|Federal Republic of Yugoslavia]], then changed its name to [[Serbia and Montenegro]] in 2003, only qualifying under that name in 2006. All of these teams are considered the predecessors of the current [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]] team by FIFA, which first qualified under that name in 2010. The other national teams that resulted from the breakup of the SFR Yugoslavia in 1992 — [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]], [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]], and [[North Macedonia national football team|North Macedonia]] — are considered distinct entities from the Yugoslavia team of 1930–1990. [[Montenegro national football team|Montenegro]] now also competes separately after independence in 2006 and [[Kosovo national football team|Kosovo]] was recognized by FIFA in 2016.}}

== Teams ==
''Note: In case there are teams with equal quantities, they will be mentioned in chronological order of tournament history (the teams that attained the quantity first, are listed first). If the quantity was attained by more than one team in the same tournament, the teams will be listed alphabetically.''

''For a detailed list of top four appearances, see [[FIFA World Cup#Results|FIFA World Cup results]].''
=== Titles ===
* Most titles: '''5''' – {{fb|BRA}} (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002)<ref name="Analyst">{{cite news |last=Furniss |first=Matt |url=https://theanalyst.com/eu/2022/09/brazil-world-cup-wins-record/ |title=Five Stars: Brazil's FIFA World Cup Wins |date=12 September 2022 |access-date=2 January 2023 |work=The Analyst}}</ref>
* Most consecutive titles: '''2'''
**{{fb|ITA|1861}} (1934–1938)<ref name="FourFourTwo">{{cite news |last=Hayward |first=Ben |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/world-cup-2022-which-teams-have-won-back-to-back-titles |title=Which teams have won back-to-back titles? |date=16 December 2022 |access-date=2 January 2023 |work=[[FourFourTwo]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Evans |first=Chris |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63873325 |title=World Cup 2022: Vittorio Pozzo's legacy and a record that is finally under threat |date=15 December 2022 |access-date=2 January 2023 |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref>
**{{fb|BRA|1889}} (1958–1962)<ref name="FourFourTwo"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Houeix |first=Romain |url=https://www.france24.com/en/sport/20221230-the-world-cups-that-made-pel%C3%A9-immortal |title=The World Cups that made Pelé 'immortal' |date=30 December 2022 |access-date=2 January 2023 |work=[[France24]]}}</ref>
* Longest gap between successive titles: '''44 years''' – {{fb|ITA|1946}} (nine editions, 1938–1982){{refn|group="note"|Uruguay (76 years) and England (60 years) have longer active streaks.}}<ref name="RSSSF" />
* Worst finish by defending champions: '''Group stage'''
** {{fb|ITA|1946}} (1950)<ref name="worst_finish">{{Cite web |last=Harmer |first=Alfie Potts |date=23 June 2018 |title=7 Worst Defending World Cup Winners |url=https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2018/06/23/7-worst-defending-world-cup-winners/ |access-date=28 March 2023 |website=HITC}}</ref>
** {{fb|BRA|1889}} (1966)<ref name="worst_finish" />
** {{fb|FRA|1974}} (2002)<ref name="worst_finish" />
** {{fb|ITA}} (2010)<ref name="worst_finish" />
** {{fb|ESP}} (2014)<ref name="worst_finish" />
** {{fb|GER}} (2018)<ref>{{cite web |date=28 June 2018 |title=World Cup 2018: Germany, struck by Curse of the Champions, hit 80-year low |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/fifa-world-cup-2018/story/world-cup-2018-germany-struck-by-curse-of-the-champions-hit-80-year-low-1271793-2018-06-28 |access-date=28 March 2023 |website=[[India Today]]}}</ref>
* Most titles won as host: '''1'''{{refn|group="note"|No national team has won the title more than once as host.}}
** {{fb|URU}} (1930)
** {{fb|ITA|1861}} (1934)
** {{fb|ENG}} (1966)
** {{fb|FRG}} (1974)
** {{fb|ARG}} (1978)
** {{fb|FRA|1974}} (1998)

=== Appearances ===
* Most World Cup appearances: '''23''' – {{fb|BRA}}, 1930–2026 (every tournament)<ref name="RSSSF">{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesw/worldcup.html |title=World Cup 1930-2022 |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=29 December 2022}}</ref>
* Most appearances in the final: '''8''' – {{fb|GER}}, 1954, 1966, 1974, 1982, 1986 and 1990 as West Germany, 2002 and 2014 as Germany<ref name="Eurosport">{{cite news |url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/world-cup/2022/who-has-lost-the-most-world-cup-finals-who-has-made-the-most-finals-without-winning-who-has-never-lo_sto9262131/story.shtml |title=Who has lost the most World Cup finals? Who has made the most finals without winning? How many finals have France lost? |date=18 December 2022 |access-date=2 January 2023 |work=[[Eurosport]]}}</ref>
* Most runners-up: '''4'''
** {{fb|GER}}, 1966, 1982, 1986 as West Germany, 2002 as Germany<ref name="Eurosport"/>
** {{fb|ARG}}, 1930, 1990, 2014, 2026
* Most runners-up but never won a title: '''3''' – {{fb|NED}}, 1974, 1978, 2010<ref name="FIFA_runners-up_never_won_title">{{cite news |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/articles/teams-reached-final-never-won-trophy-title |title=Teams to reach final but never win the World Cup |date=1 January 2026 |publisher=FIFA |access-date=20 June 2026 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260620205302/https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/articles/teams-reached-final-never-won-trophy-title |archive-date=20 June 2026}}</ref>
* Most consecutive appearances in the final: '''3'''
** {{fb|FRG}}, 1982–1990<ref name="RSSSF" />
** {{fb|BRA}}, 1994–2002<ref name="RSSSF" />
* Longest gap between successive appearances in the final: '''48 years''' – {{fb|ARG|1861}}, 10 editions, 1930–1978<ref name="RSSSF" />
* Longest gap between successive appearances at the FIFA World Cup: '''64 years''' – {{fb|WAL}}, 16 editions, 1958–2022<ref>{{cite news |last1=Grounds |first1=Ben |last2=Hughes |first2=Geraint |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/story-telling/12018/12749842/we-are-still-here-wales-64-year-world-cup-wait |title=We are still here: Wales' 64-year World Cup wait |date=18 December 2022 |access-date=2 January 2023 |work=[[Sky Sports]]}}</ref>
* Most appearances without winning a title: '''18''' – {{fb|MEX}}
* Most appearances without advancing to the second round: '''9''' – {{fb|SCO}}
* Most consecutive failed qualification attempts: '''22''' – {{fb|LUX}}, 1934–2026<ref name="RSSSF" />

==== Teams ====
* Most goals scored overall: '''247''' – {{fb|BRA}}, 1930–2026<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/most-goals-highest-scoring-teams |access-date=19 July 2026 |title=Highest-scoring teams in World Cup history |date=13 July 2026 |publisher=FIFA}}</ref>
* Most goals scored in a tournament: '''27''' – {{fb|HUN|1949}}, [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]]{{efn|in 5 games (5,4 goals/game)}}<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/articles/highest-scoring-teams-one-edition |access-date=19 July 2026 |title=Highest-scoring teams in one World Cup |date=16 July 2026 |publisher=FIFA}}</ref>
* Most goals scored in a tournament, winning team : '''25''' – {{fb|GER}}, [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]]{{efn|in 6 matches played (4,16 goals/games)}}<ref name="2026-01-31"> {{cite web |title=World Cup Champions with the Most Goals Scored |url=https://www.thesoccerworldcups.com/champions/most_goals_scored_total.php#google_vignette |website=The Soccer World Cups |access-date=31 January 2026}}</ref>
* Fewest goals scored overall : '''0''' – {{fb|IDN}} ([[1938 FIFA World Cup|1938]]){{efn|in one game played for its only appearance under the name Dutch West Indies}}, {{fb|CHN}} ([[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002]]){{efn|in three games played for its only appearance}} and {{fb|TRI}} ([[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006]]){{efn|in three games played for its only appearance}} <ref> {{cite web |title=Every nation’s top World Cup goalscorer |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/articles/every-nation-country-top-goalscorer |website=FIFA |access-date=31 July 2026}}</ref>
* Fewest goals scored in a tournament, winning team : '''8''' – {{fb|ESP}}, [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010]]{{efn|in 8 matches played (1 goal/game)}}<ref name="2026-01-31" />
* Most goals conceded overall : '''135''' – {{fb|GER}} (1934–2026){{efn|in 116 games (1,16 goal/game)}}<ref> {{cite web |title=Germany tops the FIFA World Cup all-time goals-conceded list. It shows longevity |url=https://theprint.in/sport/fifa-world-cup-2026/germany-fifa-world-cup-goals-conceded/2965892/ |website=The Print |access-date=31 July 2026}}</ref>
* Most goals conceded in a tournament : '''16''' – {{fb|KOR}}, [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]]{{efn|in 2 matches played (8 goals/match)}}<ref> {{cite web |title=Most goals conceded by a football (soccer) team in a FIFA World Cup |url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/481211-most-goals-conceded-by-a-football-soccer-team-in-a-fifa-world-cup |website=Guinness World Records |access-date=30 July 2026}}</ref>
* Most goals conceded in a tournament, winning team : '''14''' – {{GER}}, ([[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]]){{efn|in 6 games (2,33 goal/game)}}<ref> {{cite web |title=World Cup Champions with the Most Goals Conceded |url=https://www.thesoccerworldcups.com/champions/most_goals_conceded_total.php |website=The Soccer World Cups |access-date=31 July 2026}}</ref>
* Fewest goals conceded overall: '''2''' – {{fb|ANG}}, [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006]]{{refn|group=note|in 3 matches played for its only appearance (0.67 goals/match)}}<ref> {{cite web |title=Fewest goals conceded by a football (soccer) team at the FIFA World Cup |url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/484636-fewest-goals-conceded-by-a-football-soccer-team-at-the-fifa-world-cup |publisher=Guinness World Records |access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref>
* Fewest goals conceded in a tournament: '''0''' – {{fb|SUI}}, [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006]]{{refn|group=note|in 4 matches played (eliminated via [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]])}}<ref>{{cite web |title=82 days to the World Cup: Switzerland's 0 goals allowed not good enough |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/soccer/article/82-days-to-the-world-cup-switzerlands-0-goals-allowed-not-good-enough-120000011.html |website=Yahoo Sports |access-date=24 July 2026}}</ref> 
* Fewest goals conceded in a tournament, winning team: '''1''' – {{fb|ESP}}, [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026]]{{refn|group=note|in 8 matches played (0.13 goals/match)}}<ref>{{cite web |title=What is the fewest goals conceded by a World Cup-winning team? === Scores ===
* The most common score in a regular World Cup match is 1–0.{{refn|group=note|Accurate as of 9 July 2026}}<ref>{{cite web |date=9 July 2026 |title=Most common scores in World Cup history |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/articles/most-common-scores-scorelines |access-date=20 July 2026 |publisher=FIFA}}</ref>
* The most common outcomes of a World Cup final are 4–2<ref>{{cite web |last=Cons |first=Ryan |date=19 July 2026 |title=What is the most common score in a World Cup final? The answer will surprise you |url=https://en.as.com/soccer/world-cup/what-is-the-most-common-score-in-a-world-cup-final-the-answer-will-surprise-you-f202607-n/ |access-date=20 July 2026 |website=AS}}</ref> and 1–0, inclusive extra time.

=== Streaks ===
*Longest winning streak: '''11''' – {{fb|BRA}}, 2002–2006<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/articles/teams-consecutive-successive-victories-wins|title=Teams winning most successive FIFA World Cup games|publisher=FIFA|date=1 January 2025|access-date=11 June 2026}}</ref>
*Longest unbeaten streak: '''16''' – {{fb|NED}}, 2014–2026<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/netherlands-leave-2026-world-cup-16-year-old-streak-intact |title=Netherlands Leave 2026 World Cup With 16-Year-Old Streak Intact |publisher=FOX Sports |date=30 June 2026}}</ref>
* Longest unbeaten streak in regulation time (excluding extra time): '''23''' – {{fb|NED}}, 2010–2026
* Longest losing streak: '''9''' – {{fb|MEX}}, 1930–1958<ref>{{cite web|url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/world-cup-records-part-36-most-consecutive-defeats-2342|title=IFFHS MEN'S WORLD TEAM 2025|website=IFFHS|publisher=International Federation of Football History & Statistics|access-date=11 June 2026}}</ref>
* Longest winless streak: '''17''' – {{fb|BUL}}, 1962–1994<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/articles/bulgaria-longest-winless-run-record|title=Stoichkov sparkles as the Lions quench thirst|publisher=FIFA|date=27 October 2025|access-date=11 June 2026}}</ref>
* Longest drawn streak: '''5''' – {{fb|BEL}}, 1998–2002<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/484480-most-consecutive-draws-by-a-football-soccer-nation-at-the-fifa-world-cup|title=Most consecutive draws by a football (soccer) nation at the FIFA World Cup|publisher=Guinness World Records|access-date=11 June 2026}}</ref>
* Longest streak without draw: '''17''' – {{fb|FRG}}, 1966–1974
* Longest streak scoring at least 1 goal: '''18'''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/articles/teams-scored-most-successive-games|title=Teams scoring in most successive FIFA World Cup games|publisher=FIFA|date=1 June 2026|access-date=11 June 2026}}</ref>
** {{fb|BRA}}, 1930–1958
** {{fb|FRG}}, 1934–1962
** {{fb|GER}}, 1986–1998
* Longest goalless streak: '''5'''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/84439-most-football-soccer-fifa-world-cup-matches-played-consecutively-without-scorin|title=Most football (soccer) FIFA World Cup matches played consecutively without scoring|publisher=Guinness World Records|access-date=11 June 2026}}</ref>
** {{fb|BOL}}, 1930–1994
** {{fb|HON}}, 1982–2014
** {{fb|ALG}}, 1986–2010
* Longest goalless streak by minutes: '''517 minutes''' – {{fb|BOL}}, 1930–1994<ref>After the entire 1930 and 1950 editions ended without a goal, Bolivia scored their first and only goal in the 67th minute of the third match of the 1994 Group Stage.</ref>
* Longest [[Shutout#Association football|clean sheet]] streak: '''6''' – {{fb|ESP}}, 2022–2026<ref name="spaincleansheet">{{cite news|url=https://apnews.com/article/spain-simon-world-cup-shutout-streak-521ec97ae04772e40ffd6c61c08d8e07|title=Spain sets World Cup record with 6th clean sheet in a row and keeper Simón extends scoreless mark|publisher=Associated Press|date=6 July 2026|access-date=6 July 2026}}</ref>
* Longest streak without conceding a goal by minutes: '''650 minutes''' – {{fb|ESP}}, 2022–2026<ref name="650minutes"/>
* Longest streak without clean sheet: '''22''' – {{fb|SUI}}, 1934–1994<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/84437-most-consecutive-football-soccer-fifa-world-cup-matches-without-a-clean-sheet|title=Most consecutive football (soccer) FIFA World Cup matches without a clean sheet|publisher=Guinness World Records|access-date=11 June 2026}}</ref>

=== Discipline ===
{{see also|List of FIFA World Cup red cards}}
* Most red cards (tournament): '''28''' – 2006, in 64 matches<ref name="redcards_records" />
* Most red cards (all-time, team): '''11''' – {{fb|ARG}}, {{fb|BRA}}<ref name="redcards_records" />
* Most red cards (match, both teams): '''4''' – 2 each for {{fb|POR}} and {{fb|NED}}, 2006{{refn|group=note|Also known as [[Battle of Nuremberg (2006 FIFA World Cup)|Battle of Nuremberg]].}}<ref>{{cite web |last=Bailey |first=Ryan |date=17 October 2014 |title=10 Matches with a Shocking Amount of Red Cards |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2235142-10-matches-with-a-shocking-amount-of-red-cards |access-date=24 May 2023 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref>
* Most red cards (final match): '''2''' – {{fb|ARG|1861}} v {{fb|FRG}}, 1990{{refn|group=note|The players sent off were [[Pedro Monzón]] and [[Gustavo Dezotti]].<ref name="ARG_GER_1990" />}}<ref name="ARG_GER_1990">{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Jerrad |date=8 September 2013 |title=World Cup Infamy: The 5 Players Sent Off in World Cup Finals |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1765504-world-cup-infamy-the-5-players-sent-off-in-world-cup-finals |access-date=24 May 2023 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref>
* Most yellow cards (tournament): '''345''' – 2006, in 64 matches<ref>{{cite web |last=Soergel |first=Andrew |date=12 June 2014 |title=Counting the Cards at the World Cup |url=https://www.usnews.com/news/blogs/data-mine/2014/06/12/counting-the-cards-at-the-world-cup |access-date=7 June 2023 |website=U.S. News & World Report}}</ref>
* Most yellow cards (match, one team): '''10''' – {{fb|ARG}} v {{fb|NED}}, 2022<ref name="battle">{{cite news |date=10 December 2022 |title=Netherlands vs. Argentina 'Battle of Lusail' sees record 18 yellow cards |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/blog-the-toe-poke/story/4829954/netherlands-vs-argentina-world-cup-quarterfinal-sees-record-18-yellow-cards |access-date=3 February 2023 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

=== Assists ===
Notes:{{efn|The following statistics apply '''[[Assist (association football)#Opta criteria|Opta's assist criteria]]''' to every FIFA World Cup match from 1930 onward.<br/>Under Opta's criteria:<ref>{{cite web|url=https://theanalyst.com/articles/opta-football-stats-definitions |title=Opta Football Stats Definitions |date=13 July 2024 |access-date=21 July 2026 |work=The Analyst}}</ref>
* Assists are '''not awarded''' when the ball is significantly deflected or rebounded by an opposing player, altering its trajectory before reaching the goalscorer.
* Assists are '''not awarded''' for penalties, direct goals from corners or free kicks, or own goals.
While [[Opta Sports|Opta Analyst]]'s published World Cup assist records cover all tournaments from 1966 onward, these shown statistics retrospectively apply the same criteria to earlier editions, from 1930–1962, using available match footage. Where video evidence is unavailable, assists are assessed and verified from contemporary newspaper reports and detailed descriptions of the goals. Consequently, these figures may differ from those published by other sources that do not retrospectively apply Opta's criteria to pre-1966 tournaments and from Opta itself, as they treat all pre-1966 assists as non-existent in their records and statistics.}}

* Oldest goalkeeper to keep a clean sheet: '''{{Age in years and days|1949|9|18|1990|6|26}}''' – [[Peter Shilton]] for {{fb|ENG}} v {{fb|BEL}}, 26 June 1990<ref>{{Multiref |{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/17/76/323/55 |title=England vs Belgium {{!}} Round of 16 {{!}} 1990 FIFA World Cup Italy |publisher=FIFA |access-date=1 May 2026}} | {{cite web |url=http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/round=323/match=55/index.html |title=1990 FIFA World Cup Italy – Matches – England v Belgium |publisher=FIFA |access-date=1 May 2026 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171214163049/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/round=323/match=55/index.html |archive-date=14 December 2017}} }}</ref>

=== Discipline ===
* Fastest yellow card: '''13 seconds''' – [[Jesús Gallardo]], for {{fb|MEX}} v {{fb|SWE}}, 2018<ref>{{cite news |date=27 June 2018 |title=Mexico yellow card fastest in World Cup history |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/mexico/story/3547297/jesus-gallardos-yellow-card-for-mexico-fastest-in-world-cup-history |access-date=28 January 2023 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>
* Fastest red card: '''56 seconds''' – [[José Batista]], for {{fb|URU}} v {{fb|SCO}}, 1986<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/2014/6/world-cup-rewind-jos%C3%A9-batista-clocks-up-the-fastest-ever-sending-off-57934 |title=World Cup Rewind: José Batista clocks up the fastest ever red cards |publisher=Guinness World Records |date=9 June 2014 |access-date=24 December 2022}}</ref>
* Fastest red card, qualification: '''37 seconds''' – [[Rashed Al-Hooti]], for {{fb|BHR}} v {{fb|IRN}}, 11 October 2011, [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification]]<ref>{{cite news |last=Marioni |first=Massimo |date=12 October 2011 |title=Rashed Al Hooti gets the 'fastest international red card ever' for Bahrain |url=https://metro.co.uk/2011/10/12/rashed-al-hooti-gets-the-fastest-international-red-card-ever-for-bahrain-182121/ |access-date=28 January 2023 |newspaper=Metro}}</ref>
* Latest yellow card: '''During penalty shoot-out''' – [[Emiliano Martínez]], for {{fb|ARG}} v {{fb|FRA}}, 2022{{refn|group=note|Putting French players off.<ref name="emiliano_martinez" />}}<ref name="emiliano_martinez">{{Cite news |last=Glendenning |first=Barry |date=19 December 2022 |title=Emiliano Martínez: shootouts, controversy and World Cup success |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/dec/19/emiliano-martinez-shootouts-controversy-and-world-cup-success |access-date=24 May 2023 |newspaper=The Guardian}}</ref>
* Latest red card: '''After penalty shoot-out'''
** [[Leandro Cufré]], for {{fb|ARG|1861}} v {{fb|GER}}, 2006{{refn|group=note|Cufré was [[Penalty card#Red card|red carded]] for kicking [[Per Mertesacker]] in an altercation following the [[2006 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Germany vs Argentina|match]].<ref name="cufre" />}}<ref name="cufre">{{cite news |last=Jackson |first=Jamie |date=1 July 2006 |title=Pekerman ethos blown up in a fit of emotion |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/jul/02/worldcup2006.sport16 |access-date=24 May 2023 |newspaper=The Guardian}}</ref>
** [[Denzel Dumfries]], for {{fb|NED}} v {{fb|ARG}}, 2022<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bettoni |first=Lorenzo |date=10 December 2022 |title=Why Inter star Dumfries was sent off in Argentina-Netherlands |url=https://football-italia.net/why-inter-star-dumfries-was-sent-off-in-argentina-netherlands/ |access-date=24 May 2023 |website=Football Italia}}</ref>
* Sent off from the bench – [[Claudio Caniggia]], for {{fb|ARG|1861}} v {{fb|SWE}}, 2002<ref>{{cite news |date=26 June 2022 |title=Caniggia hit by ban and fine |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport3/worldcup2002/hi/team_pages/argentina/newsid_2067000/2067942.stm |access-date=24 May 2023 |work=BBC News}}</ref>
* Most cards: '''7''' – [[Javier Mascherano]], {{fb|ARG}}, 2006–2018<ref name="Mascherano">{{cite news |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/mascherano-makes-unwanted-world-cup-history-as-argentina-bow-out-/pdqvz713x41p1kpvpsrpjvaq8 |title=Mascherano makes unwanted World Cup history as Argentina bow out of Russia 2018 |last=Burton |first=Chris |website=Goal.com |access-date=1 July 2018 |archive-date=30 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630225559/http://www.goal.com/en/news/mascherano-makes-unwanted-world-cup-history-as-argentina-bow-out-/pdqvz713x41p1kpvpsrpjvaq8 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Most yellow cards: '''7''' – [[Javier Mascherano]], {{fb|ARG}}, 2006–2018<ref name="Mascherano" />
* Most yellow cards in a match: '''3''' – [[Josip Šimunić]], 61', 90', 93', for {{fb|CRO}} v {{fb|AUS}}, 2006, by referee [[Graham Poll]]{{refn|group=note|Šimunić was given three yellow cards in the match as the referee failed to send him off the pitch after the second yellow, and was only red carded after the third yellow.<ref name="three_yellows">{{cite news |date=20 November 2022 |title=FIFA World Cup: When referee Graham Poll mistakenly gave three yellow cards to Croatian defender Josip Simunic in 2006 |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/uk/fifa-world-cup-when-referee-graham-poll-mistakenly-gave-three-yellow-cards-to-croatian-defender-josip-simunic-in-2006/articleshow/95641709.cms?from=mdr |access-date=28 January 2023 |newspaper=The Economic Times}}</ref>}}<ref name="three_yellows" />
* Most red cards: '''2'''
** [[Rigobert Song]], for {{fb|CMR}}, 1994 and 1998<ref name="redcards_records">{{Cite web |last=Ibrahim |first=Mina |date=25 November 2022 |title=History, records, controversy: Everything you need to know about World Cup red cards |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3914522/2022/11/25/world-cup-red-card-history/ |access-date=28 January 2023 |website=The Athletic}}</ref>
** [[Zinedine Zidane]], for {{fb|FRA|1974}}, 1998 and 2006<ref name="redcards_records" />
* Most suspensions in a tournament: '''2''' – [[André Kana-Biyik]], for {{fb|CMR}}, 1990{{refn|group=note|Biyik missed the team's second game after receiving a red card in the first,<ref>{{cite news |last=Dove |first=Ed |date=27 November 2022 |title=Cameroon 1990: Celebrating Africa's World Cup pioneers |url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/lists/cameroon-1990-celebrating-africa-s-world-cup-pioneers/blt8da5407090ceef78 |access-date=7 June 2023 |website=Goal.com}}</ref> and then missed Cameroon's fifth game after yellow cards in the third and fourth.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cameroon vs. Soviet Union - Football Match Summary - June 18, 1990 |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/197987 |access-date=7 June 2023 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cameroon vs. Colombia - Football Match Summary - June 23, 1990 |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/198009 |access-date=7 June 2023 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> Others, including [[Zinedine Zidane]] in [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006]], have earned a second suspension in their team's final match of the tournament, not servable during the tournament.}}<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pagani |first=Francesco Federico |date=22 May 2010 |title=FIFA World Cup records: i record Mondiali! |url=https://sciabolatamorbida.wordpress.com/2010/05/22/fifa-world-cup-records-i-record-mondiali/ |access-date=7 June 2023 |website=Sciabolata Morbida |language=it-IT}}</ref>

* Most matches coached: '''27''' – {{flagicon|FRA}} [[Didier Deschamps]], for {{fb|FRA}}, 2014–2026{{refn|group=note|name=deschamps|Including one group stage match at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], a 4–1 win over [[Norway national football team|Norway]], when Deschamps was temporarily represented by his assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hill |first=Courtney |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/fifa-world-cup-2026-france-head-coach-didier-deschamps-miss-norway-game |title=FIFA World Cup 2026: France head coach Didier Deschamps to miss Norway game |publisher=International Olympic Committee |date=24 June 2026 }}</ref><ref name="Analyst_postmatch_fra_mor_qf2026">{{cite news |last=Carr |first=Harry |url=https://theanalyst.com/articles/france-vs-morocco-stats-world-cup-2026-quarter-final |title=France vs Morocco Stats: World Cup Quarter-Final - Opta Analyst |date=9 July 2026 |access-date=10 July 2026 |work=The Analyst}}</ref><ref name="fifa_deschamps">{{Cite news |date=6 July 2026 |title=Didier Deschamps leaving his mark on Les Blues|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/articles/didier-deschamps-changed-everything-for-france |access-date=10 July 2026 |publisher=FIFA }}</ref>}}
* Most matches won: '''20''' – {{flagicon|FRA}} [[Didier Deschamps]], for {{fb|FRA}}, 2014–2026{{refn|group=note|name=deschamps}}
* Most tournaments won: '''2''' – {{flagicon|ITA|1861}} [[Vittorio Pozzo]], for {{fb|ITA|1861}}, 1934–1938<ref>{{Cite web |last=Evans |first=Chris |date=15 December 2022|title=World Cup 2022: Vittorio Pozzo's legacy and a record that is finally under threat |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63873325 |access-date=23 December 2022 |website=BBC Sport }}</ref>
* Most tournaments as a coach: '''6''' – {{flagicon|BRA}} [[Carlos Alberto Parreira]], for {{fb|KUW}} in 1982, for {{fb|UAE}} in 1990, for {{fb|BRA}} in 1994 and 2006, for {{fb|KSA}} in 1998 and for {{fb|RSA}} in 2010<ref name="Parreira">{{cite web|url=https://www.correiobraziliense.com.br/app/noticia/superesportes/2009/12/08/interna_superesportes,159715/parreira-nao-teme-marca-negativa-nas-copas.shtml |title=Parreira não teme marca negativa nas Copas |website=Correio Braziliense |date=8 December 2009 |language=pt |access-date=23 December 2022}}</ref>
* Most different nations coached: '''5'''
** {{flagicon|SER}} [[Bora Milutinović]], for {{fb|MEX}} in 1986, for {{fb|CRC}} in 1990, for {{fb|USA}} in 1994, for {{fb|NGA}} in 1998 and for {{fb|CHN}} in 2002<ref name="Milutinovic"/>
** {{flagicon|BRA}} [[Carlos Alberto Parreira]], for {{fb|KUW}} in 1982, for {{fb|UAE}} in 1990, for {{fb|BRA}} in 1994 and 2006, for {{fb|KSA}} in 1998 and for {{fb|RSA}} in 2010<ref name="Parreira" />
* Most consecutive tournaments as a coach: '''5'''
** {{flagicon|SER}} [[Bora Milutinović]], 1986–2002<ref name="Milutinovic">{{Cite news |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/behind-the-world-cup-record-bora-milutinovic-2890944 |title=Behind the World Cup record: Bora Milutinovic |publisher=FIFA |date=7 September 2020 |access-date=7 September 2020 |archive-date=7 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200907103955/https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/behind-the-world-cup-record-bora-milutinovic-2890944 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
** {{flagicon|POR}} [[Carlos Queiroz]], 2010–2026<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/ghana-coach-enters-record-books-his-fifth-world-cup-row-2026-06-15/ |title=Ghana coach enters record books at his fifth World Cup in row |publisher=Reuters |date=15 June 2026 }}</ref>
* Most consecutive tournaments as a coach with the same team: '''4'''
** {{flagicon|ENG}} [[Walter Winterbottom]], for {{fb|ENG}}, 1950–1962<ref name="coach_same">{{Cite web |title=The coach at the most editions |url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/world-cup-records-part-26-the-coach-at-most-editions-2307 |access-date=26 December 2022 |website=IFFHS}}</ref>
** {{flagicon|FRG}} [[Helmut Schön]], for {{fb|FRG}}, 1966–1978<ref name="coach_same" />
** {{flagicon|FRA}} [[Didier Deschamps]], for {{fb|FRA}}, 2014–2026<ref name="coach_same" />
* Youngest coach: '''{{Age in years and days|1902|10|21|1930|7|15}}''' – {{flagicon|ARG}} [[Juan José Tramutola]] for {{fb|ARG|1861}} v {{fb|FRA|1794}}, 15 July 1930<ref>{{Cite news |title=Youngest coach in a FIFA Women's World Cup |url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/379936-youngest-coach-in-a-fifa-womens-world-cup |access-date=25 December 2022 |publisher=Guinness World Records }}</ref>
* Youngest coach of a World Cup winning team: '''{{Age in years and days|1898|11|20|1930|7|30}}''' – {{flagicon|URU}} [[Alberto Suppici]] for {{fb|URU}}, 1930<ref>{{cite web |last=Pavlović |first=Svetozar |date=15 December 2022 |title=Which team won the first World Cup? When and where was it played? |url=https://en.as.com/soccer/which-team-won-the-first-world-cup-when-and-where-was-it-played-n/ |access-date=26 December 2022 |website=Diario AS}}</ref>
* Oldest coach: '''{{Age in years and days|1947|9|27|2026|6|25}}''' – {{flagicon|NED}} [[Dick Advocaat]] for {{fb|CUW}} v {{fb|CIV}}, 25 June 2026<ref>{{cite web |last=Kane |first=Evan |date=14 June 2026 |title=World Cup's oldest manager is back with his Curaçao family |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/worldcup/2026/06/14/dick-advocaat-curacao-germany-smallest-country/90549113007/ |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=USA Today}}</ref>
* Oldest coach of a World Cup winning team: '''{{Age in years and days|1961|6|21|2026|7|19}}''' – {{flagicon|ESP}} [[Luis de la Fuente (footballer, born 1961)|Luis de la Fuente]], for {{fb|ESP}}, 2026<ref> {{cite web |title=Guiness World Records on X |url=https://x.com/GWR/status/2078975811663626524 |website=X |access-date=20 July 2026}}</ref>
* Oldest-living coach: '''{{Age in years and days|22 June 1933}}''' – '''{{flagicon|BRA}}''' [[Evaristo (footballer)|Evaristo]] for '''{{flagicon|IRQ}}''', 1986
* Longest-lived coach: '''{{Age in years and days|31 July 1916|24 March 2020}}''' – '''{{flagicon|MEX}}''' [[Ignacio Trelles]], 1962 and 1966
* Oldest-living winning coach: '''{{Age in years and days|16 March 1938}}''' – '''{{flagicon|ARG}}''' [[Carlos Bilardo]], 1986
* Longest-lived winning coach: '''{{Age in years and days|9 August 1931|5 January 2024}}''' – '''{{flagicon|BRA}}''' [[Mário Zagallo]], 1970
